lines.en: I can count the amount of “dates” I went on with my Maya on one hand. Though I’m not sure she’d call them that if she were still here today.
Since she’s not, though, I feel as if I can safely label that night at the takoyaki stand as our first without incurring any more ghostly wrath than I already do on a nightly basis.
Come to think of it, a second haunting might be nice — even if I doubt Maya and Sekai would get along very well.
They wouldn’t need to, though. I’m sure I could figure out how to ration my time in between the secret resurrection studies I’ve been partaking in behind your back.
It’s only a matter of time now. Not until I succeed — until I become one of them. And there’s no longer any need to study at all.
But it’s precisely because it’s a matter of time that I feel confident when I tell you it is so far away that you’ll likely be gone before I reach it.
And I probably won’t remember ever telling you this at all.
There’s a hand to my side that doesn’t belong to me.
It keeps brushing up against mine as if it’s asking for something — but it’s an unwelcome sensation that does little but annoy me and cause me to move aside by half a step.
Not enough to make it obvious that I’m rejecting it, but enough to reject it while still leaving room for a little wishful thinking to fill her thoughts in place of my appendage.
This is only our second first-date after all. It’s only right to wait at least one more before we touch.
Which ignores all of the angry, begrudging sex I have already had with her. But that’s something else I’m trying to look past too.
I just won’t know what sorts of wonders a second first-fuck will be until after the second first-date.
But will a second first-box and the encroaching second first-meal we’ll share dilute or distort any of these new memories to the point where keeping them isn’t worth the risk?
I wonder if she asked herself the same thing when she was taking me here?
How annoying it is to have the roles reversed.
No wonder why she was always so angry.
: Do you want anything?
: You mean you’ll let me buy myself food with my own money?
: I think I’m supposed to. That seems like proper date etiquette to me.
The old man behind the counter grunts. I doubt I’ll ever hear anything else from him.
: We could also go out to a restaurant instead if you’d rather-
: No. It has to be here.
: Has to? Why does it have to be here?
The old man grunts again.
: And why does he keep doing that?
: It’s how he communicates, I think. Like Yasu with her incessant ramblings about God and...old Maya with her incessant ramblings about how disgusting I am.
: She had a point. You are pretty disgusting.
: Don’t say that line. You haven’t earned it yet.
: Are you seriously telling me I have to earn the right to say my own lines? Because I get being enamored, but this is just sad.
: Then, to even the playing field, I hereby grant you permission to ban me from saying one thing your version of me frequently said to you. That way, we’ll both be happy.
: Great. Then I hereby ban you from saying “no.” Would you like to go fornicate behind a tree now?
: No.
: You bastard. You’ve already broken the rules.
: This agreement was voided from the get-go since there’s basically no way I’d have ever said “no” to you to begin with.
: I’m sure it happened once or twice.
The old man grunts again, this time with slightly more fervor or feeling than before.
: Oh. I guess we should probably order.
: That is what we’re supposed to do here, yes. But it’s not like this guy has anything else going on. He probably enjoys the-
Another grunt. Something tells me I will die after the next.
: Just give us the usual please.
: There’s only one thing on the menu. I think this is more of a quantity problem than him not knowing what to give us.
: Then — enough to feed five to ten girls, please.
: You’re not planning on inviting others, are you?
: No. I just know you well and don’t feel like spending enough to feed twenty girls. Ten seemed like a fair compromise.
: How very kind of you. Perhaps once we’re done, I’ll let you fornicate with me behind a tree completely free of charge.
: Are you a prostitute now?
: Yes. Please hurry, takoyaki man. I’m a poor high school girl and I need to go have sex with this adult man for money.
: I’d be worried if I wasn’t partially convinced this guy is actually a robot.
: I’m not entirely convinced that we’re all not actually robots. And that our whole lives are some weird simulation about AI obtaining actual intelligence or something.
: My Maya’s theories were way better than that. And that’s saying a lot since practically all of them were wrong.
: I take great offense to this. If there is anything I know about myself, it is that I am always right. And if there is anything I know about you-
A fifth grunt from the old man. This is where I die.
Or perhaps just relocate to a bench to continue feeding into the undeniable yet tragically painful chemistry I have with this creature.
For it truly feels as if we have known each other forever. But this forever has only lasted a little over a year.
And while that’s more than many get, it’s hard to say it feels like anything when I never thought that Maya was going to leave me in the first place.
Even with all of the warnings that are now...racing back to me in hindsight.
That isn’t all that’s racing back, though. There’s hope, too. There’s-
: Feed me.
: Feed me and I’ll let you fornicate with me behind a tree.
: What is it with you and this tree thing all of a sudden?
: I don’t really know. The first time was just a joke but, the more I say it, the more it sounds kind of fun.
: You can also just feed me without the promise of sex, though. Anything to get those hot balls inside of my mouth.
: Yeah, I think this date thing was actually a bad idea after all.
: Fine. Then you leave me no choice but to revert to my former self since that is the one you have apparently decided to latch onto.
: Assuming of course that a man of your supreme idiocy and undeniable general grossness is capable of latching onto any one thing to begin with.
: Which implies, of course, that I believe I’d be extremely well fed if only I was an entire group of teenagers rather than just one unfortunate, yet immensely adorable girl.
: You’re disgusting.
: Fine. I’ll feed you so long as it gets you to stop trying to be her.
: Wait. Now I’m confused. Don’t you want me to be her? Isn’t that your entire goal in talking to me again?
: It’s...a little more complicated than that.
: I’m very interested in whatever that might possibly mean. But I’m also very hungry and I don’t know which feeling to prioritize.
: Well you can take your time if- oh. I guess you’ve already figured it out.
: Food now, talk later. I have made up my mind.
: At least we know there’s no food in those mysterious boxes since I imagine you would have found a way to tear them open earlier.
: Aaaaaaah~
: Aaaaaaaahhhhh~
: AAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHH!
: Sorry. This just...feels really weird.
: To be completely honest, I agree. We’re being so cute right now that I imagine we must look like an actual couple.
: I think you’re doing the heavy lifting in the cuteness department. I’m kind of just...here.
: True. I didn’t want to be the one to say it, though.
: But on the bright side, at least being next to me makes you look better.
: Or worse when you’re telling strangers that I’m paying you to have sex with me.
: Doubtful. A girl like me could bring in a lot of money, Sensei. People might think you’re rich if I keep telling them that.
: It’s a vast departure from that whole “pretend we don’t know or like each other” thing. But hey, I got used to that and I can get used to this too.
: Did I...really make you do that?
: Well...yeah. It’s not like you forced it on me, though. It was my idea.
: But why would you-
: It’s just easier that way. You don’t have to deal with people knowing your proclivities and I don’t have to deal with a parade of teenagers also trying to bone you.
: You mostly just mean Ami, don’t you?
: I mostly just mean Ami, yes.
: But now she knows fucking everything ever and you’re fucking everyone ever, so...why bother continuing to handicap myself?
: Especially if you’re going to, like...try to see me more...and stuff.
: You really suffered for me, didn’t you?
: Not until you started fucking ignoring me, asshole. This whole “suffering” thing is still new to me.  And, I’ll tell you what, Sensei- I’m not cut out for it.
: Well, I’ve got bad news for you then. Because-
: Yeah, whatever. Before you start with that whole “just being with me is suffering” nonsense, let me remind you that you’ve been saying that forever and it has literally never been an issue.
: Unless you’ve, like...actually been cheating on me this entire time and were just really good at hiding it. But I’m pretty sure that’s, like a...your world thing.
: Wait, so...you’re conceding that this world is my world? That you’re not supposed to be here?
: Now- I didn’t say that I’m not supposed to be here. But with all of the weird shit that’s been happening and everything I’ve heard from you and Ayane?
: It’s pretty much impossible to convince myself at this point that the world is what I thought it was.
: You should applaud me for how perceptive and smart I am now.
: Sorry...it’s just...
: It’s weird that you can...know this much despite not having been to the rooftop with us.
: You shouldn’t have retained any of that, Maya. Everything Ayane and I told you should have been purged after Halloween.
: Ugh. I wish it was. Everything’s so...weird now. And...scary.
: But I...care less about that right now and...more about just getting you back.
: Because you are my coping mechanism, Sensei. You are the box I’ve stored all of my feelings in. And there’s not a chance in hell I could confront any of this without you.
: You...want to confront it then?
: Well, to be fair, I still don’t really know what it is we’re confronting. But yes. Whatever it is, I want to do it with you.
: I’m just...
: Hah...
: All this...paranormal stuff if...that’s what you want to call it...
: It’s all making me feel less...permanent than I want to feel.
: Like...what if I do get to keep going? What if you fall back in love with me? And everything’s normal and good again and you stop sleeping with other girls.
: Maya-
: Shut up. I’m not done.
: What if all of that happens and you lose me again? Or I lose you? Or we both get lost somehow? Or, even worse, what if you never stop sleeping with other girls?
: Maya-
: Again, shut up. You seriously need to stop interrupting me. And also sleeping with other girls.
: Oh. If you can’t tell, I’m also really annoyed that you keep sleeping with other girls.
: I...had a feeling.
: Point is, Sensei...there’s still so much I don’t know. And I don’t want you to put too much faith into me getting it just because I’ve gotten it in the past or...future?
: I don’t know where...your me is from on a technical level. But it kind of sounds like both in a way?
: I think it kind of is both in a way. Because she existed before you chronologically, but then obviously lasted way longer than you have.
: What do you think was happening with my consciousness in the meantime then?
: I don’t know, but...I imagine the other Maya would have come up with something about timelines or...yeah. You were probably just...somewhere else.
: ...Somewhere else, huh?
: Yeah...or something like that.
: Has that...ever happened to you, Sensei?
: Have you ever just...been somewhere else all of a sudden? Or maybe...some...when else?...
: Probably...yeah.
: It’s kind of...hard to remember, though. Like...it seems like it’s there but...fuzzy.
: Do you want to remember? Or do you think everything would just get even more confusing if you did?
: Everything always gets more confusing here. That’s just the way this world works, I think.
: That’s another thing I’m afraid of. Because I know you’re hoping somewhere deep down that I will remember things that happened with the me who isn’t me.
: And while I know that might feel real to you...for me, I...
: Well...
: You know...I often wish I didn’t have to remember Sekai.
: Well, duh. That’s basically the only reason we’re together.
: But I often also think that one day, remembering her might actually be good. And I might become stronger for it.
: HA! No you don’t, you fucking liar! The day you’re that optimistic about anything is the day I give up watermelon.
: Heh...you’re right.
: Wouldn’t it be nice if you weren’t, though?
: Yeah. But I think there are a lot of things out there that would be nice. And that chances are, we won’t ever get to see or experience the vast majority of them.
: Well hey, that’s one potential perk of an infinite life if we’re able to hang on. We might actually get to see...everything.
: Yeah...maybe.
: But then what?...
: What else is there to see when we’ve already seen everything? What else is there to do when we’ve already done it all?
: Is that the end of the world?
: Is that what she saw?
: I don’t think so...
: The end of the world is a little more colorful than that.
There’s a hand to my side that doesn’t belong to me.
But when it reaches for something that does — a cardboard boat of fried octopus that is likely only somewhat scorching now — I do something.
I grab it.
Her hand — not the takoyaki.
And when I grab it, there’s this...pause.
Silence.
She stares down at our hands for a moment, the same as me, and my mind once again gravitates to the size disparity between the two.
But then she tilts her head up and her eyes meet mine.
And we just sit there for a full minute looking at each other.
We aren’t smiling. We aren’t speaking.
We’re just...connecting.
And it’s the most unfaithful I have ever felt.
